blocks.text: Rain moves across the windows. Axiom Tower is visible from almost every room, which is either convenient or deliberate.
Benton said the deputy director decision would be waiting this morning. For three years, I have done half the job without the title. Today is supposed to correct that.
Your phone lights up on the counter. Maya’s message waits beneath the time.
Drinks tonight? And don’t tell me you’re working late. Again.
blocks.speaker: Maya · message

blocks.text: Maya Reyes. Corporate compliance investigator. We met during my first year at Axiom. A decade of bad coffee, sealed investigations and knowing when the other person is lying. She is not my boss. What she means to me is harder to name.
She is my closest friend.
blocks.speaker: Adrian

blocks.text: Maya is the closest thing I have to family inside Axiom.
Drinks tonight? And don’t tell me you’re working late. Again.
blocks.speaker: Maya · message

blocks.text: The message is still waiting for an answer.
Absolutely.
blocks.speaker: Adrian

blocks.text: Message sent: “Absolutely.”
Your jacket waits in the closet. Beyond the windows, Axiom Tower remains framed by the rain.

You pocket your phone and pull on your usual coat. Outside, rain gathers along the curb. Axiom Tower disappears behind the nearer buildings, then rises above you as you join the employees filing through its doors.

Most of the lobby belongs to security. Glass partitions channel the morning queue into screening lanes beneath a bank of cameras. Uniformed guards watch the scanners; beyond them, a second line of locked gates separates the public entrance from the elevators.

You set your phone and coat in a tray, pass your employee badge over the reader and wait on the floor marker while the camera checks your face. A guard watches your belongings move through the scanner. Only when both checks clear does the gate release.
Eleven years. I still wait for the green light before reaching for my things.

You collect your coat and phone, then badge through the inner gate. The elevator carries you to Strategic Intelligence. When its doors open, voices and the low hum of terminals reach you. Daniel is waiting beside your desk.

Daniel Kessler is waiting beside your desk, making no effort to pretend the meeting is accidental. Thirty-two, long-limbed and permanently one button short of Axiom’s dress code, he has dark curls that resist corporate grooming and a face that usually gives away the joke before he tells it. There is no joke this morning.
He lowers his voice. “They gave it to Priya. Benton says you’re too valuable where you are.”
blocks.speaker: Daniel Kessler

blocks.text: Daniel has worked two desks over from me for four years. Clever, indiscreet, kinder than he wants anyone to notice. I am grateful he told me himself—and angry that I am hearing it from him instead of Benton.
“Priya earned it.”
blocks.speaker: Adrian

blocks.text: Daniel nods. “Sure,” he says, in a tone that means he believes none of it.
blocks.speaker: Daniel

blocks.text: Daniel pushes away from the desk divider and leaves you with the news. Before you can sit, the smoked-glass door of the director’s office opens. Elias Benton crosses the intelligence floor carrying a thin black data slate. Conversations soften as he passes.

Benton is fifty-eight, compact and silver-haired, his charcoal suit so precisely fitted that it seems less like clothing than policy. He never hurries. He has built a career out of making everyone else adjust their pace to his.
He stops at the edge of your desk rather than calling you into his office. “Vale. Helix is buying Novagen Bio. I need the acquisition logic and risk exposure before lunch. Keep it narrow.”
blocks.speaker: Director Elias Benton

blocks.text: Benton has supervised me for four years. He praises precision when it protects him and calls it overthinking when it does not. He has not mentioned the promotion, and his arrival makes disappointment harden into suspicion. He almost never brings an assignment to someone’s desk himself.
“You will have it before lunch.”
blocks.speaker: Adrian

blocks.text: Benton gives one economical nod. “Good. You’ve always understood priorities.” He places the data slate on your desk and turns away.
blocks.speaker: Benton

blocks.text: I said yes before asking why he came in person. His approval still works on me more quickly than I care to admit.
Benton returns across the floor to his office. The Helix acquisition file wakes on the slate. Deadline: 12:00. Distribution: Benton only.

Helix Corporation is acquiring Novagen Bio. Benton’s brief gives a simple rationale: Helix wants its adaptive-cell patents. The deal sponsor is Marcus Chen, Helix Director of Strategic Acquisitions. Benton wants a narrow risk note before lunch.

Marcus Chen buys distressed companies, keeps what Helix values and sells the remains. I know the reputation, not the man. His name alone does not make this unusual. Benton carrying the file to my desk does.
Your task is to assess the acquisition logic. Establish what the records prove before deciding what they mean.
Each source can establish a fact, repeat a claim or introduce uncertainty. Read at least two records before analysis. You can keep reviewing the documents while you work.
Read Acquisition request — Benton claims Helix wants Novagen for its patents. Authenticates what Benton said, not that he believes it or that the rationale is true.

Read Helix divestiture 8-K — Helix sold comparable patents six months ago and accepted a five-year reacquisition restriction. Establishes the transaction and restriction, not Helix’s present acquisition motive.
Read Novagen seeks strategic buyer — Outside analysts value Novagen mainly for personnel and clinical relationships. An outside valuation is not direct evidence of Helix’s intent.

Read Helix talent activity — The intelligence note records Helix contacting Novagen personnel before the announcement. Recruiting activity is documented; its relationship to the acquisition remains an inference.
Select two records you have read, then describe their relationship. Experimenting is free. You can retry, ask for a hint, investigate once, or review an assessment for submission.
Benton wants an answer, not a catalogue. But an answer built on the wrong relationship is worse than admitting I do not know.

Connection supported. The filing challenges Benton’s stated patent rationale: Helix disposed of comparable patents and restricted reacquisition. This does not prove Helix’s actual motive, Benton’s beliefs, or wrongdoing.

The morning has narrowed to the minutes left before lunch. Review your conclusion and attachments below. Submitting sends them to Benton and closes this investigation. You can still revise before committing.
The report leaves your terminal addressed to Benton only. Your selected conclusion remains in it, with the records and connections you chose to attach.

The recorded divestiture and reacquisition restriction conflict with Benton’s patent rationale. The records do not establish Helix’s actual motive. Your assessment separates the problem in the stated rationale from a motive the evidence does not establish.

Maya Reyes crosses from the compliance wing carrying two paper cups. Thirty-three, with warm brown skin and watchful dark eyes, she wears her black hair in a loose knot and has turned back the cuffs of her navy suit. The small rebellion suits her. She sets one cup beside your terminal and keeps the other. No greeting. This is an old ritual.
Maya is the closest thing I have to family inside Axiom. She knows when I am lying before I decide to lie. Seeing her now loosens something in my chest I did not realize I was holding.
“Daniel told me about Priya. And before you start defending everyone involved—how are you?”
blocks.speaker: Maya Reyes

blocks.text: “I thought this one was mine.”
blocks.speaker: Adrian

blocks.text: Maya’s expression softens. “I know. It should’ve been yours.”
blocks.speaker: Maya

blocks.text: “You said absolutely this morning. I am checking that you still mean it.”
blocks.speaker: Maya

blocks.text: “Come out tonight. One drink. Try being a person instead of an Axiom function for an hour.”
blocks.speaker: Maya Reyes

blocks.text: “Eight o’clock.”
blocks.speaker: Adrian

blocks.text: “Eight,” she says. “I am holding you to that.”
blocks.speaker: Maya

blocks.text: Her eyes catch the Helix and Novagen names on the report header. The details are not visible from where she stands.
“Helix and Novagen? Compliance cleared that as routine two weeks ago. Why is Benton putting Strategic Intelligence on it now?”
blocks.speaker: Maya Reyes

blocks.text: That is Maya at work. She does not ask what I found. She asks why the system wanted me looking.
“Benton told me to keep it narrow.”
blocks.speaker: Adrian

blocks.text: Maya studies you. “That was not an answer. It was a warning.”
blocks.speaker: Maya

blocks.text: She taps the desk twice. “Eight o’clock. Do not disappear.”
blocks.speaker: Maya

blocks.text: I am relieved she came. Whatever else the day has taken, it has not taken that.
Maya lifts her coffee and steps away from the desk. You watch her start back toward the compliance wing before returning to your terminal.
The space beside your desk is quiet again. You take a sip of coffee. It is still warm. The Helix report has already left your hands.
The first part of the opening is complete. Your decisions and the information you chose to share remain on the record. Review them here, or continue Adrian’s day when you are ready.
Your choice: Continue Adrian’s day
Six minutes after Maya leaves, the Helix report minimizes without input. A different case appears in its place. You did not put it there, and its access classification is higher than yours.
Files do not wander into Axiom Intelligence by accident. Someone placed this in my queue. I do not yet know who, or why.
EV_7A_BLACKGLASS. Origin: unresolved. Owner: A. Vale. Status: present in your workspace. The ownership field is a system label, not an explanation.
Your hand rests beside the mouse. The cursor is still exactly where you left it over the Helix report. Whatever brought this here did not need you to move it.
This morning I wanted someone to notice my work. Now a file I should not be able to see is carrying my name, and the floor around me sounds entirely normal.
Reporting, deleting and tracing the object do not open its protected contents. You can also leave without authorizing access. That ends this route with the anomaly unresolved.
Your choice: Open the directory
Most of the directory is encrypted. Four identifiers remain visible.
ORACLE — predictive system; clearance denied. PROJECT EVE — adaptive identity program; status active. VOSS, LENA — Axiom Adaptive Medicine. VALE, ADRIAN — Candidate 7A; identity package ready.
My name is not on an assignment. It is on a candidate record.
You read the surname again, then the given name. There is no other analyst you can mistake it for. You lean toward the screen before realizing you are trying to shield it from the rest of the floor.
Candidate for what? The directory offers a place for my hand where an explanation should be.

The Adrian Vale record requests biometric authorization. You should not possess clearance, but the palm reader is waiting. Authorizing would attach your biometric signature to an attempt to open the restricted record. Closing the directory gives no such authorization.
Voss is listed in Adaptive Medicine. I have no earlier personnel connection to compare with this directory.
Your choice: Authorize with palm reader
You place your palm on the reader. ACCESS GRANTED. CANDIDATE 7A — ACTIVE. E.VALE IDENTITY PACKAGE — READY.
The record begins to open. Before the image resolves, your terminal locks. The office lights shift from white to security amber. Conversations stop behind you.
The authorization line stays. With your free hand, you press Escape once. Nothing happens. The voice behind you arrives before you can decide whether to try again.
“Mr Vale, take your hand off the reader. Leave your badge on the desk.”
blocks.speaker: Axiom Security

blocks.text: Your choice: Turn around

Two officers stand behind your chair. The nearer one is a broad-shouldered woman in her forties, copper-brown hair clipped close and a matte security badge fixed precisely beneath her collarbone. Her younger partner has a narrow face, pale lashes and both hands visible at his sides. Neither reaches for a weapon. She takes your badge while he disconnects the terminal.
I have never seen either of them on this floor. Familiar faces might invite negotiation. Fear arrives first, cold and physical. Anger follows quickly enough to let me speak.
“Mr Vale, you are being escorted to Executive Intelligence. You are not under arrest.”
blocks.speaker: Senior security officer

blocks.text: “That sentence usually ends well.”
blocks.speaker: Adrian

blocks.text: The senior officer holds out a steady hand for your phone. Beyond the glass partition, Maya has stopped in the compliance corridor. You cannot tell how much she has seen.
You glance from the officer’s hand to your phone. She follows the movement without stepping closer.
“If you need to notify someone, one message. In front of me. Then the phone.”
blocks.speaker: Senior security officer

blocks.text: A permitted message is not a private one. Maya could know where I have gone. They would know who I reached for.

You can surrender the phone, demand an explanation, or send Maya one warning first. Sending it would identify her to the officers as someone you are involving. The message will say only: “SECURITY HAS ME. THEY ARE TAKING ME TO EXECUTIVE INTELLIGENCE.”
Your choice: Give them the phone and cooperate
You surrender the phone. You send Maya nothing. She watches from the corridor as the officers lead you away.

The younger officer brings your coat from the back of your chair. You take it before the officers escort you off the floor. The elevator display changes to EXECUTIVE INTELLIGENCE — LEVEL 71. It ignores every floor in between.
“Employee access status: suspended pending executive review.”
blocks.speaker: Axiom system

blocks.text: The younger officer watches the floor numbers. The senior one watches your reflection in the doors. You straighten your coat over your arm because it gives your hands something ordinary to do.
My apartment, medical coverage and corporate accounts all use that identity. Suspension is not termination. It is enough to show me how much of my life is behind their gates.
At Level 71, the senior officer delivers your phone in a sealed pouch to an executive aide. You hear the aide confirm receipt for Director Sloane. The officers lead you to her door.
Your choice: Enter Sloane’s office

Victoria Sloane stands at the window with the city spread beneath her. She is in her late forties, tall and spare, with bronze skin, black hair cut cleanly at the jaw and a single silver streak at her right temple. Her graphite suit carries no department pin or visible rank. It does not need one. She pours herself water, turns, and leaves you standing.
The office is beautiful without being comfortable: dark wood, pale stone, no family photographs. No interrogation lights. No recording equipment you can see.
The aide closes the door. Sloane leaves the chair opposite her desk empty. You remain beside it, aware of the coat folded over your arm and how much you suddenly want somewhere to put it.

I have never met Sloane. Everyone in Strategic Intelligence knows her name: Director of Executive Intelligence, sealed operations, careers ended by unsigned reviews. I expected menace. Her calm is worse. I am afraid—and angry that she can probably see it.
“Do you know what disappoints me about you, Adrian? You are very good at discovering things. You are remarkably bad at understanding why you were allowed to discover them.”
blocks.speaker: Victoria Sloane

blocks.text: Your choice: “Am I under arrest?”
“Not yet. Whether this becomes a criminal matter depends on what happens next.”
blocks.speaker: Sloane

blocks.text: Sloane slides an access audit across the desk. It records your biometric authorization, the restricted directory identifiers and the attempted opening of Candidate 7A.
“This supports immediate termination and referral for corporate espionage.”
blocks.speaker: Victoria Sloane

blocks.text: It records that I opened the record. It does not prove I put the file there or intended to steal anything. A public allegation could still end my career before a tribunal decided the difference.
“You have the moment I touched the reader. Where is the record of how the file reached my desk?”
blocks.speaker: Adrian

blocks.text: Sloane turns the audit slightly so it faces you squarely. She does not bring up another window.
“That is the question you would be trying to answer while this one was being circulated.”
blocks.speaker: Sloane

blocks.text: She has not answered me. She has described how long I might have to live without an answer.
Your choice: “If the evidence is enough, why am I here?”
“Because I need you working.”
blocks.speaker: Sloane

blocks.text: “Helix has an intelligence source inside this company. Marcus Chen, their director of strategic acquisitions, will meet that source tomorrow night at the Glass House.”
blocks.speaker: Victoria Sloane

blocks.text: Marcus Chen—the Helix executive sponsoring the Novagen acquisition. This morning he was a reputation attached to a file. Sloane is describing him as an active intelligence threat.
You have her account of a planned meeting. You have not seen independent evidence for it. You may question her before asking for the assignment.
She finally gestures to the chair. You put down the coat and sit. The courtesy feels timed: now that she has given you something to solve, she expects you to stay.
A source. A meeting. A gap in the information. My mind starts arranging them before I can stop it. She has found a way to make the work familiar while everything around it is wrong.
Your choice: “What exactly do you want me to do?”
“Enter the Glass House. Identify Marcus’s source. Return with proof. You cannot attend as Adrian Vale.”
blocks.speaker: Victoria Sloane

blocks.text: “Then this conversation is over.”
blocks.speaker: Adrian

blocks.text: “Evelyn Vale already has an invitation.”
blocks.speaker: Victoria Sloane

blocks.text: The name lands without an explanation. Sloane lets the silence after it last, then turns the display toward you.
E.VALE. The identity package in the file. I assumed it was another operative. Sloane says the name as if I should recognize it.
She opens the record where Security interrupted it. A woman appears beside a government identity, eight years of financial records, an Axiom employment history and photographs labelled Singapore.

Evelyn looks thirty-one: shoulder-length dark hair swept behind one ear, an ivory jacket cut with severe elegance, and a composed expression that suggests the photographer has interrupted something more important. The face is feminine but not alien. She has your eyes, the line of your cheekbones and the slight asymmetry at one corner of your mouth.

You look away from the screen and back again. It does not become a stranger the second time. One detail will seem almost familiar, then the whole face will slip out of recognition. You cannot decide which is worse.
I recognize myself in her before the overlay appears. The first feeling is violation. The second is harder to name. I do not trust Sloane enough to show her either.

AXIOM IDENTITY PACKAGE: EVELYN VALE. Age 31. Strategic Acquisitions. Glass House clearance. Singapore location history. Status active. The overlay claims 99.97 percent compatibility across facial structure and projected biometrics. These are Axiom’s records and calculations; you have no way to authenticate them here.
“You made her from me.”
blocks.speaker: Adrian

blocks.text: “Yes.”
blocks.speaker: Victoria Sloane

blocks.text: “Who is she?”
blocks.speaker: Adrian

blocks.text: “You are.”
blocks.speaker: Victoria Sloane

blocks.text: You feel your jaw tighten. For a moment you are conscious of your own face as something other people can inspect: the skin at your cheek, the weight of your mouth, the expression you are failing to control.

She has said two words as if that settles ownership. I am sitting here. The woman is on a screen. I need time to understand what she is asking me to connect, and Sloane is already watching for my answer.
Your choice: Keep looking at Evelyn
You keep looking at the photograph. Sloane watches your gaze; you have not told her what it means.
At 07:00 tomorrow, Axiom Adaptive Medicine would begin a Stage One physical adaptation to make you pass as Evelyn at the Glass House.
“Tomorrow? You expect me to leave here, go home, and come back ready for that?”
blocks.speaker: Adrian

blocks.text: You gesture at the screen. Sloane looks at your hand, then at your face.
“Stage One is mostly reversible. Dr Lena Voss will explain the medical limits before the procedure. You will identify the source and obtain proof of the exchange.”
blocks.speaker: Victoria Sloane

blocks.text: Mostly. There is a whole unanswered question inside that word. She has given it to tomorrow’s doctor, along with the parts of this conversation she does not want to have.
“And if I say no?”
blocks.speaker: Adrian

blocks.text: “I send the audit to Corporate Security. You lose your position today. Your lease subsidy ends in thirty days. They decide whether to prosecute. Complete the operation, and the breach disappears.”
blocks.speaker: Victoria Sloane

blocks.text: “That is blackmail.”
blocks.speaker: Adrian

blocks.text: “Yes.”
blocks.speaker: Victoria Sloane

blocks.text: The admission takes the argument out of the room. You had expected a euphemism you could pull apart. She folds her hands and leaves you with the actual choice.
Accepting would buy time under her terms. It would not make those terms voluntary. Refusing would let me leave this room, not erase the allegation.
Your choice: Accept the operation
You accept. Sloane opens the sealed pouch delivered by the aide and places your confiscated phone beside a temporary badge with a red restriction stripe. Your ordinary work access remains suspended.
“Assume every call made on that phone is monitored. Your temporary badge will take you home and bring you back tomorrow. Sublevel 17. Seven o’clock.”
blocks.speaker: Victoria Sloane

blocks.text: “And until then?”
blocks.speaker: Adrian

blocks.text: “That is your problem to solve.”
blocks.speaker: Victoria Sloane

blocks.text: The phone feels familiar. It no longer feels private. Maya’s name is still in it. So is every unfinished promise I made this morning.

An aide escorts you to the elevator. Downstairs, a guard checks the restriction stripe against the exit reader before releasing you through the outer gate. Outside, you pull on your coat and join the afternoon traffic toward home.
Your choice: Go home
Your temporary badge admits you to the residential building. The door closes behind you. You set the phone on the counter, then move it farther away.

The apartment has not changed. There is the cup you left by the sink, the ordinary crease in the cushion, the tower beyond the windows. You had expected the room to make you feel like yourself again. Instead it shows you how little time has passed.
I could still be deciding what to say to Maya about the promotion. That was a real hurt this morning. It has not stopped being one just because something larger arrived.
For a while you stand where you watched the tower this morning. You eat without tasting much. The rain stops. Afternoon becomes evening without making the appointment feel any less real.
Your choice: Let the hours pass
Axiom Tower remains framed in the windows, every lit floor reflected faintly in the glass. You have taken off your coat but not your shoes. Evelyn’s photograph is still open behind your eyes.
Tomorrow morning. Not now. Twelve hours in which I am still Adrian Vale, with no idea what to do with them. The phone can reach Maya. Sloane told me to assume it also lets Axiom listen.
“I saw them take you off the floor. Are you home? Please tell me you’re all right.”
blocks.speaker: Maya · message

blocks.text: There is still the promise of eight o’clock beneath the more urgent question.
Maya is the person I call when the world stops making sense. I am afraid of what calling her might cost.
Your choice: Call Maya from the apartment

At 19:03, you call from the apartment. Maya answers on the second tone. Her hair is down and the light behind her is warm. You warn her that Axiom may record the call. “Then I should know that before you speak,” she says.
Neither of you speaks at first. She adjusts the phone so she can see you properly, then leaves it still. You can hear a little room noise from her end. It makes the distance feel more exact.
“I saw the escort. I couldn’t tell whether following would make it worse.”
blocks.speaker: Maya

blocks.text: She is giving me the time I could not get upstairs. Somehow that makes it harder to begin.
“You look like somebody explained your life to you and got all the important parts wrong. What happened?”
blocks.speaker: Maya

blocks.text: I trust her. The question is how much danger arrives with the answer. I can tell her about the appointment, explain the detention, or try to pass it off as work.
Your choice: “Axiom ordered me to Adaptive Medicine at seven tomorrow.”
“Adaptive Medicine, at seven? Was that a request, or an instruction?”
blocks.speaker: Maya

blocks.text: She lowers her voice, though both of you know that would make no difference to a recording.
“An instruction.”
blocks.speaker: Adrian

blocks.text: Maya takes a breath through her nose and lets it out slowly.
“I can listen without making this a case. I cannot help you with something you won’t name.”
blocks.speaker: Maya

blocks.text: She has given me another chance to trust her. I can give her a way to check on me, tell her about Evelyn, or ask her to stop. None of those choices will make her unhear what I have already said.
Your choice: “Call me at 06:30. If I don’t answer, look for Sublevel 17.”
Maya sets an alarm for 06:29.
“I call you at six-thirty. If you don’t answer, I start with Sublevel 17 and work outward.”
blocks.speaker: Maya

blocks.text: “I’ll answer.”
blocks.speaker: Adrian

blocks.text: She studies you for a moment before nodding. Neither of you treats it as a small promise.
Relief comes with guilt. I have given her a way to find me, and a reason to go looking.

There are a few quieter minutes after that. You ask how the rest of her day went and listen to her choose an ordinary answer. Neither of you is fooled by the change of subject. Neither tries to stop it.
At 19:18 you say goodbye. The call ends. Your own reflection remains where Maya’s face had been. You are still in your apartment.
Your choice: Finish the evening
Maya will call at 06:30. You have promised to answer. The arrangement gives the morning another deadline.

The evening is over. You are alone in the apartment again. The phone lies face-down on the kitchen counter. There is an appointment you have agreed to attend, and no guarantee beyond Sloane’s word about what follows.
You check the time more often than it changes. Once, you walk to the window with the intention of closing the curtains and leave them open. The tower gives you somewhere to look.
Your choice: Set the phone down

Notifications are muted. The phone’s Axiom filter says unidentified senders are blocked. It chimes anyway: two clean electronic notes, high then low. You start hard enough to strike your knee against the counter. The screen wakes by itself.
For one irrational second I expect Sloane’s name. There is no name—only a sender field filled with static.
DON’T GO TO SUBLEVEL 17.
blocks.speaker: Unknown sender

blocks.text: You turn the phone over, as though the source might be on the other side. When you look again, the line is still there. The room is quiet enough to hear your own breathing.
Your choice: Keep reading
Three seconds pass. The phone gives the same two-note chime, quieter now that it is in your hand. A second line appears without a typing indicator.
AND DON’T TRUST THE WOMAN IN THE PHOTOGRAPH.
blocks.speaker: Unknown sender

blocks.text: Evelyn? Whoever sent this appears to know about the appointment and a photograph. Are they trying to save me, or redirect me?
Your choice: Wait for the sender
No chime accompanies the third message. The words simply appear beneath the others.
SHE ISN’T YOU.
blocks.speaker: Unknown sender

blocks.text: Sloane said Evelyn is me. This stranger insists she is not. I have a claim from each of them, and no way to test either tonight. I lock the phone, then unlock it immediately, as if the words might change.
Your choice: End Adrian’s day
The three messages remain on the phone. You do not know who sent them. The appointment is still set for 07:00, Sublevel 17.
Morning is close. I have agreed to go. That is not the same as knowing whom to believe.
Adrian’s day ends here, before the clinic. Review the information you earned and the choices you made, or save this run for the next milestone.
Your choice: Begin the next morning

The alarm finds you awake. Rain has thinned to a pale mist across the window, and Axiom Tower has begun exchanging its night lights for the colder light of occupied offices. For several seconds you watch a floor illuminate without remembering which part of yesterday should frighten you first.

The phone lies face down beside the bed. You turn it over. The three messages are still there; reading them in daylight has not supplied a sender or an explanation. Beneath them, the appointment remains fixed at 07:00.
I can decide what to do with a warning. I cannot make it true by needing it to be true.

Your jacket hangs where you left it. In its pocket, the temporary badge presses a narrow rectangle into the lining. The familiar weight of your keys is beside it. You wash, dress, and leave the apartment door closed while you gather yourself. There is still a little time before six-thirty.
Your choice: Let six-thirty arrive
At exactly six-thirty Maya’s name fills the screen. You asked her to make this call. Answering it would keep the promise; letting it ring would leave her with the uncertainty you agreed to spare her.
Yesterday I wanted one person to know where I was going. Wanting that does not make the phone private.
Your choice: Answer Maya’s call
Maya. I’m here. This phone is still monitored.
blocks.speaker: Adrian

blocks.text: I remember. Are you leaving for Sublevel 17?
blocks.speaker: Maya

blocks.text: Yes. The appointment is at seven. I wanted to answer before I went.
blocks.speaker: Adrian

blocks.text: Her relief arrives as a breath before she finds the words. You hear the ordinary sounds of her morning behind it, and for a moment that is harder than the questions.
Then you kept this part of the promise. Tell me when you can speak again.
blocks.speaker: Maya

blocks.text: I will try. I can’t promise when.
blocks.speaker: Adrian

blocks.text: All right. Goodbye, Adrian.
blocks.speaker: Maya

blocks.text: You say goodbye and wait until the call has ended before lowering the phone.
Your choice: Leave the apartment

You check the stove although you have not used it, then collect the phone, keys, and restricted badge. Your hand stays on the apartment door after the lock engages. Tonight you may come back through it differently. The corridor gives you no place to put that thought.

Downstairs, you join the morning transit queue. Nobody knows where your appointment is. A woman beside you balances a takeaway cup over her bag; two analysts argue softly about a meeting. You recognize the relief of having a small problem and feel briefly ashamed of envying them.
The tower grows wider between the buildings. At its entrance you straighten your jacket, an old habit surviving the loss of the access it once suggested.
Your choice: Enter Axiom

The lobby is already busy. Beyond the doors, three security lanes divide staff from visitors. Cameras follow each approach before anyone reaches a reader. You put the temporary badge against the glass and watch the employee lane remain closed.
Appointment access. Adaptive Medicine. Use the staffed lane, please.
blocks.speaker: Entrance officer

blocks.text: The officer is broad through the middle, with close-cropped grey hair and a patient expression that does not invite familiarity. You have passed this desk for years without needing his attention. Today he compares your face with a terminal image, checks the appointment, and asks you to place the phone in a shallow tray.
Does this get me back to my floor?
blocks.speaker: Adrian

blocks.text: Transit and residential access. The appointment adds one escorted destination. Your office is not on it.
blocks.speaker: Entrance officer

blocks.text: He says it as though he is reading the weather. There is nothing here I can argue with that will change the reader.
Your choice: Place the phone in the screening tray

The scanner carries the phone beneath a dark cover. A second display compares the device identifier with the one registered to your badge. You can see the phone throughout; the few seconds still feel like another confiscation.
Take your phone. Elevator four will accept the appointment. It will not offer you another floor.
blocks.speaker: Entrance officer

blocks.text: You check the familiar nick at the edge of the case before putting it away. The officer returns the temporary badge and opens the pedestrian gate. You pass through only after the indicator turns green.
Elevator four has no ordinary floor menu for you. ADAPTIVE MEDICINE appears above a single confirmation field. You select it, and the doors close on the working day upstairs.
Your choice: Take the phone and descend

The elevator opens onto white stone, warm wood, and light designed to resemble morning. Nothing smells medical. Water moves quietly behind a wall of ribbed glass. Someone has worked very hard to prevent the place from feeling underground.
The receptionist wears a cream uniform and has a silver pen fastened neatly inside her sleeve. She looks up with a practiced welcome, sees your badge, and pauses.
Good morning, Mr Vale. Dr Voss is expecting you.
blocks.speaker: Receptionist

blocks.text: Her terminal turns slightly as she reaches for a pass. You read PATIENT: VALE, EVELYN before she straightens it.
Yesterday it was a photograph. Here it is a patient waiting to be admitted. I am the person they have to fit into the record.
Your choice: “Why is the patient record under Evelyn?”
Why is the patient record under Evelyn?
blocks.speaker: Adrian

blocks.text: That is the linked treatment identity. Dr Voss will explain the appointment. I cannot amend the clinical record from reception.
blocks.speaker: Receptionist

blocks.text: Her answer gives the label a function without explaining its origin.
The receptionist opens the inner door. You follow the lit passage to the examination suite, still carrying your phone and badge.
Your choice: Enter the examination suite

Dr Lena Voss waits beside an examination chair. She is slight and sharp-featured, in her mid-forties, with silver threading the dark hair at her temples. A charcoal blouse shows beneath her open medical coat. She closes a record before greeting you, then looks at your face rather than your badge.
She looks tired. I want that to mean there is a conscience keeping her awake. Exhaustion can belong to anyone.

Sloane stands beside a window that displays a convincing imitation of daylight. Her clothes look as immaculate as they did yesterday. You have spent the intervening hours trying to sleep; she gives no sign that the interval mattered.
You told him?
blocks.speaker: Voss

blocks.text: Enough.
blocks.speaker: Sloane

blocks.text: That was not my question.
blocks.speaker: Voss

blocks.text: Voss turns toward the chair but does not ask you to sit yet.
I need to assess my patient. Privately.
blocks.speaker: Voss

blocks.text: Sloane remains beside the window. Both women wait, and the room becomes yours in one very limited respect: someone expects you to say who may remain in it.
Her name was in the directory, and Sloane named her as the doctor. This is the first time I have met the person behind it.
Your choice: “I would prefer medical privacy.”
“I would prefer medical privacy.” Sloane pauses before stepping outside. Voss closes the door herself.
The baseline scan is measurement only. We will discuss adaptation afterward.
blocks.speaker: Voss

blocks.text: You have a private interval with Voss. It does not make the rest of the appointment private.
Your choice: Begin the baseline examination

The chair adjusts beneath you with a series of almost inaudible movements. Voss tells you where to put your hands before the scanner approaches. Its ring passes slowly around your shoulders, close enough that you have to resist drawing them inward.
This is measurement. No adaptation has started. Tell me if the position becomes uncomfortable.
blocks.speaker: Voss

blocks.text: Columns move on her terminal: tissue density, endocrine response, skeletal tolerances. She reads them quickly, then returns to a number you cannot see. You try to read her hesitation and remember that you are an analyst attempting to assess a doctor by the angle of her head.

Three details are within reach of your attention: the reflected procedure record, a calibration seal on the array, and your historical scan data. The scan gives you time to inspect one. You may also let it finish without investigating.
Optional examination opportunity: 1. Inspect one source; its result will appear immediately. Rereading and follow-up questions are free.
Your choice: Inspect the reflected procedure record
Examination opportunity remaining: 0.
The procedure record assigns Stage One medical authority to Voss. Later stages are locked behind separate affirmative authorization.
There are two authorities on the page. That distinction may matter when they stop agreeing.
You can reread this finding here or in the journal. The inspection cannot be spent again.
Your compatibility is high. The adaptation should be stable.
blocks.speaker: Voss

blocks.text: How long have you known that?
blocks.speaker: Adrian

blocks.text: That is a better question for Victoria.
blocks.speaker: Voss

blocks.text: She releases the chair and helps you return to the consultation area.
Your choice: Return to the consultation area
Voss opens the door and calls Sloane back. She returns before the protocol discussion begins.

Voss lowers the wall display until its labels sit at eye level. The model is clinical rather than theatrical: a sequence of tissue, endocrine, skeletal, and voice adaptations grouped under STAGE ONE. Later stages remain separately locked.
Today is intended to produce social and biometric viability. The full program would take months. I am not authorizing that program today.
blocks.speaker: Voss

blocks.text: Victoria said mostly reversible.
blocks.speaker: Adrian

blocks.text: Most of the soft-tissue changes can be reversed through further treatment. Your endocrine baseline will not reset on command. Recovery has its own demands. And I cannot remove your memory of the experience.
blocks.speaker: Voss

blocks.text: She lets the last sentence remain in the room. Sloane looks at the schedule on her own display.
You have an evening planned for me before you have even started.
blocks.speaker: Adrian

blocks.text: She has an operation planned. I still have a patient to assess. Those are different responsibilities.
blocks.speaker: Voss

blocks.text: Yesterday “mostly” was a word Sloane moved past. Voss has put it on the table. I am not sure whether that makes her safer or simply more exact.
Your choice: Review the operational profiles

Four versions of the same face replace the medical model. The differences are restrained: emphasis, line, presentation. The eyes and the asymmetry at one corner of the mouth persist. None offers the possibility of becoming an unrelated person.
The existing Evelyn already has an invitation.
blocks.speaker: Sloane

blocks.text: The optional parameters stay within that identity’s recognition tolerances. He can choose them.
blocks.speaker: Voss

blocks.text: Sloane touches the original, then takes her hand away. Voss turns the controls toward you. For the first time the interface is arranged for your reach rather than someone else’s.
A choice within a design I did not commission. Small is not the same as meaningless. It is also not the same as freedom.
You can retain the established profile or adjust it toward executive authority, social warmth, or an understated operative presentation. Reviewing a profile does not commit it.
Your choice: Review the existing Evelyn profile
Selected preview: existing.
The original looks exactly like the photograph Sloane presented. You remember the angle at which she held the screen and how long it took you to look away.
Nothing has been applied to your body. Confirm this profile or return to compare another.
Your choice: Confirm this profile

The display places a live image of you beside the predicted result. Both figures shift when you breathe. Evelyn does not move like a recording; she waits with your impatience, holding her shoulders in the position you have held since entering the room.

The resemblance refuses to stay in one category. Your eyes are familiar until the surrounding face changes how you read them. A small movement of the mouth carries an expression you recognize from photographs you dislike.
I can look at a prediction without promising to want it. I need to remember that before someone writes down the length of my attention.
This is a model. There will be variation during recovery. Tell me what you need to understand.
blocks.speaker: Voss

blocks.text: Sloane says nothing. The rendering lights her face as well as yours.
Your choice: Study Evelyn’s face
The uneven corner of the mouth catches your attention again. You almost touch your own mouth to compare them, then notice Sloane and leave your hand where it is.
Well?
blocks.speaker: Sloane

blocks.text: She has let the silence go on just long enough that I want to fill it.
Your choice: Remain silent
Adrian remained silent after the simulation.
Before I begin, I need your authorization for Stage One. Your agreement to an operation is not permission for me to start a procedure.
blocks.speaker: Voss

blocks.text: And if I refuse here?
blocks.speaker: Adrian

blocks.text: The arrangement ends. The referral and employment consequences we discussed proceed.
blocks.speaker: Sloane

blocks.text: And I do not begin. If you ask me to stop after we have begun, I stop further adaptation and assess what is needed to stabilize you. That will not mean I can return you to your starting condition today.
blocks.speaker: Voss

blocks.text: Voss places the authorization control within your reach. There is no countdown. Beside it, the selected profile and the limits you have discussed remain available for review.
The threat has not disappeared because someone has explained the procedure carefully. But the hand that starts it must still be mine.
Stage One only. Mostly reversible through further treatment, not an immediate reset. Later irreversible stages require separate affirmative authorization. You may review, authorize, or refuse.
Confirmed profile: existing. Authorization status: not yet given.
Your choice: Refuse Stage One

Voss keeps the procedure inactive while you consider the decision. Sloane states that ending treatment ends the mission arrangement: the security referral proceeds, employment is terminated if it has not already been, and the housing subsidy moves to the threatened thirty-day notice. A notice already issued does not start again.
Those consequences do not authorize further treatment. If you end it, I arrange recovery and continuing care for your actual condition.
blocks.speaker: Voss

blocks.text: Confirming ends this clinic route. Going back returns to the authorization or paused checkpoint; it does not restart treatment.
Physical stage: No adaptation begun.
Going back does not restart the equipment.
Your choice: Confirm: end further adaptation
Voss confirms the stop on her terminal before turning to Sloane.
There will be no further adaptation. I am transferring care to recovery.
blocks.speaker: Voss

blocks.text: Then the operation arrangement is withdrawn. The referral proceeds.
blocks.speaker: Sloane

blocks.text: Sloane leaves after recording the administrative instruction. Voss calls the recovery nurse, explains your condition in your presence, and asks you to correct anything that does not match what you are feeling. The nurse brings a chair alongside yours.

The recovery handover includes an administrative notice confirming employment termination and the housing subsidy change. If a thirty-day notice was already issued, its original deadline remains. No appointment or route back to the operation is imposed. You remain in clinical recovery, with continuing care and discharge arrangements pending.
Physical stage: No adaptation begun.
Your phone, keys, jacket, and restricted badge remain with you. No invitation credentials or earpiece are issued.
